questions.question: After an upgrade to Australia, a CMDB manager wants analysts to work in CMDB tables that used to require the itil role, without giving them itil. Which role does the Australia release make sufficient for those tables?

options.text: sn_cmdb_admin
sn_cmdb_editor
sn_cmdb_user
app_service_admin

explanation.correct: In the Australia release, access to CMDB tables is no longer restricted to users with elevated privileges: CMDB tables that required the itil role are now also accessible to the sn_cmdb_editor user role, so analysts can do the work with a role trimmed to CMDB features. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Australia notes pair sn_cmdb_admin with tables that required the admin or itil_admin roles, not with tables that required the itil role.

As of Zurich the itil role contains sn_cmdb_user, and the notes say functions that were accessible to itil users now require the sn_cmdb_editor user role, so sn_cmdb_user is not enough; Australia opens itil-only CMDB tables to sn_cmdb_editor.
app_service_admin still contained the itil role until Brazil removed it, so granting it in Australia would give analysts itil; the Australia change opens itil-only CMDB tables to sn_cmdb_editor.

source.excerpt: CMDB tables that required the itil role are now also accessible to the sn_cmdb_editor user role.

questions.question: An administrator is upgrading an instance directly from Yokohama to Australia. What must the administrator do so that user roles such as CMDB Admin and CMDB Editor are configured correctly?

options.text: Run the scheduled job that removes CMDB roles from ITIL roles
Add the itil role to the sn_cmdb_admin and sn_cmdb_editor roles
Download the latest CMDB Workspace store app from the Store
Apply the cmdb_ci composite index guidance in KB2588894 first

explanation.correct: The Australia upgrade information says that if you're upgrading from Xanadu or Yokohama directly to Australia, you must run the 'Remove CMDB Roles from ITIL roles and Add CUD access to sn_cmdb_admin/sn_cmdb_editor roles' scheduled job to correctly configure user roles such as CMDB Admin and CMDB Editor. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The scheduled job does the opposite: it updates the itil role to no longer contain sn_cmdb_editor (and itil_admin to no longer contain sn_cmdb_admin) and gives the CMDB roles create, update, and delete access to cmdb_ci.
Downloading a newer CMDB Workspace store app is how you get the latest workspace features; the release notes do not say it configures the CMDB Admin and CMDB Editor roles.
KB2588894 covers the increased Australia upgrade time caused by the cmdb_ci composite index addition, not the configuration of CMDB roles.

documentation.section: Configuration Management Database (CMDB) - Important information for upgrading

source.excerpt: If you're upgrading from Xanadu or Yokohama directly to the Australia release, you must run the Remove CMDB Roles from ITIL roles and Add CUD access to sn_cmdb_admin/sn_cmdb_editor roles scheduled job to correctly configure some user roles, such as CMDB Admin and CMDB Editor.

questions.question: A company has a newly zBooted Brazil instance and also upgrades an existing instance that uses Static IRE to Brazil. How does the Brazil release handle Dynamic IRE on the two instances?

options.text: On by default when zBooted; upgraded one can switch to it
On by default when upgraded; zBooted one must activate it
Off on both until an administrator activates a plugin
On by default on both, with Static IRE converted for good

explanation.correct: The Brazil upgrade information states that Dynamic IRE is now enabled by default on zBooted instances, while on upgraded instances that are using Static IRE you can switch into using Dynamic IRE. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This reverses the documented behavior: Dynamic IRE is enabled by default on zBooted instances, and upgraded Static IRE instances are the ones that can switch.
Dynamic IRE is enabled by default on zBooted Brazil instances, so it is not off everywhere pending a plugin activation.
Upgraded instances that use Static IRE are not converted automatically; the release notes say you can switch into using Dynamic IRE.

documentation.section: Configuration Management Database (CMDB) - Important information for upgrading

source.excerpt: Dynamic IRE is now enabled by default on zBooted instances, while on upgraded instances that are using Static IRE you can switch into using Dynamic IRE.

questions.question: After upgrading to Australia, a CMDB admin sets glide.identification_engine.lookup_match.create_duplicate_task_ci.enabled to true. During lookup-based identification, two serial number records are identical but each references a different CI. What does IRE do?

options.text: Matches the older CI and creates a de-duplication task
Matches the older CI but creates no de-duplication task
Matches the newer CI and creates a de-duplication task
Rejects the payload and logs an identification error

explanation.correct: Australia added the option to have IRE create de-duplication tasks for duplicate related items in a lookup table, controlled by glide.identification_engine.lookup_match.create_duplicate_task_ci.enabled. When it is true, IRE selects the older CI for the matching process and generates a de-duplication task to remediate the duplication. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/id-detect-dup-ci.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: That is the false (default) behavior: IRE selects the older CI as a match but doesn't create a de-duplication task. With the property set to true, a task is generated.
In this situation IRE selects the record with the older referenced CI as the match, not the newer one.
IRE does not reject the payload; it selects the record with the older referenced CI as a match in the identification process.

source.excerpt: Configure IRE to create de-duplication tasks for duplicate related items in a lookup table, detected during a lookup-based identification.

questions.question: After upgrading to Australia, a CMDB admin wants saved CMDB Query Builder queries that contain OR operators to run in V2 engine mode. Which system property controls the engine mode for these queries?

options.text: glide.cmdb.query.execution_mode
glide.cmdb.query.max_results_limit
glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode
glide.cmdb.query.query_time_limit_in_sec

explanation.correct: The Australia release notes say OR operators can't run in V2 engine mode unless explicitly enabled by the glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode system property. That property sets the system-wide default engine mode for queries that contain at least one logical OR condition, and it has precedence over glide.cmdb.query.execution_mode. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/configuration-management-database-cmdb/query-builder-engine-execution-mode.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: glide.cmdb.query.execution_mode sets the default engine when a query's mode isn't set, but for queries with OR conditions glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode has precedence over it.
glide.cmdb.query.max_results_limit limits the number of results for a scheduled query or Load All Results; it does not choose the engine mode.
glide.cmdb.query.query_time_limit_in_sec is the time limit for running an entire query; it does not choose the engine mode.

source.excerpt: Query structures that aren't supported include related list conditions, NOT operators combined with filters, certain Service Mapping relationships, and OR operators unless explicitly enabled by the glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode system property.

questions.question: An administrator at a service provider has a domain-separated instance, upgrades it to Australia, and wants to know which CMDB tables gained domain separation support in that release. Which two tables are listed? (Choose two.)

options.text: Key Value [cmdb_key_value]
Configuration Item [cmdb_ci]
Client Access [samp_client_access]
Serial Number [cmdb_serial_number]

explanation.correct: Under 'Domain separation for key CMDB tables', the Australia release notes list Key Value [cmdb_key_value], Printer Instance [cmdb_print_queue_instance], Software Instance [cmdb_software_instance], Client Access [samp_client_access], and Oracle Options [samp_oracle_options] as tables that now support domain separation. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] is not one of the five tables in the Australia list of tables that now support domain separation (Key Value, Printer Instance, Software Instance, Client Access, Oracle Options).

Serial Number [cmdb_serial_number] is not one of the five tables in the Australia list of tables that now support domain separation (Key Value, Printer Instance, Software Instance, Client Access, Oracle Options).

source.excerpt: The following tables now support domain separation on instances which are configured with domain separation: Key Value [cmdb_key_value] ... Client Access [samp_client_access]

questions.question: After the Australia upgrade, a CMDB analyst finds that the Multisource Report Builder is gone. Which tool do the release notes point to for generating reports on multisource data?

options.text: CMDB Health dashboard in CMDB Workspace
CMDB 360 in CMDB Workspace
Saved queries in CMDB Query Builder
Dashboards in CMDB success advisor

explanation.correct: The Australia deprecation notes say the Multisource Report Builder has been removed and to use CMDB 360 in CMDB Workspace or in Service Graph Workspace to generate reports for multisource data. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes do not name the CMDB Health dashboard as the replacement for multisource reports; they direct you to CMDB 360.
CMDB Query Builder saved queries are not the documented replacement; the notes name CMDB 360 for multisource data reports.
CMDB success advisor dashboards target Data Foundations, HAM, and SAM data-quality outcomes; they are not the documented tool for multisource data reports.

source.excerpt: The Multisource Report Builder has been removed. Use CMDB 360 in CMDB Workspace or in Service Graph Workspace to generate reports for multisource data.

questions.question: A CMDB team that adopted Service Graph Workspace in Australia is planning its Brazil upgrade. What do the Brazil release notes say about Service Graph Workspace?

options.text: It replaces CMDB Workspace, which is removed in this release
It is deprecated, and CMDB Workspace gets its features
It takes over CMDB 360 reporting from CMDB Workspace
It moves into the Data Catalog store application

explanation.correct: Under 'CMDB Workspace merged with Service Graph Workspace features', the Brazil release notes state that Service Graph Workspace is deprecated as of this release and that CMDB Workspace will have Service Graph Workspace features. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The direction is the reverse: Service Graph Workspace is deprecated and CMDB Workspace takes on its features. The Brazil release still includes an installation of CMDB Workspace.

CMDB 360 is documented in CMDB Workspace (the Australia notes direct multisource reporting to CMDB 360 in CMDB Workspace), and in Brazil Service Graph Workspace is deprecated rather than gaining features.
The Brazil notes merge Service Graph Workspace features into CMDB Workspace; they say nothing about moving it into Data Catalog.

source.excerpt: Service Graph Workspace is deprecated as of this release. CMDB Workspace will have Service Graph Workspace features.

questions.question: In Brazil, an administrator gives a service owner the app_service_owner role instead of the broader itil role. What does that user get from app_service_owner?

options.text: View access but no edits to Service Instance records
CRUD on Service Instance records plus app_service_user
Create, update, and delete access to the entire cmdb_ci class
Access to the incidents and changes linked to each CI

explanation.correct: The Brazil release notes say to use the app_service_owner role to grant create, read, update, and delete access to Service Instance records without granting the broader itil role, and that the app_service_owner role also includes the app_service_user role. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: app_service_owner grants create, read, update, and delete access to Service Instance records, so it is not limited to viewing them.
Full create, update, and delete access to the Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] class is what the sn_cmdb_admin and sn_cmdb_editor roles receive, not app_service_owner.
The Brazil notes state that viewing related items for a CI, such as linked incidents or changes, still requires the itil role.

source.excerpt: Use the app_service_owner role to grant create, read, update, and delete access to Service Instance records without granting the broader itil role. The app_service_owner role also includes the app_service_user role.

questions.question: After upgrading to Brazil, an administrator reviews the app_service_admin role and sees that it no longer contains the itil role. Which two roles replace itil within app_service_admin? (Choose two.)

options.text: sn_cmdb_editor
sn_cmdb_admin
app_service_user
itil_admin
app_service_owner

explanation.correct: Under 'Itil role removed from app_service_admin', the Brazil release notes state that the sn_cmdb_editor and app_service_user roles replace the itil role within the app_service_admin role. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: sn_cmdb_admin is not one of the roles named as replacing itil inside app_service_admin; the notes name sn_cmdb_editor and app_service_user.
itil_admin is not named as a replacement; the notes name sn_cmdb_editor and app_service_user.
app_service_owner is the separate Brazil role for Service Instance CRUD access (it includes app_service_user); it is not one of the roles that replace itil within app_service_admin.

source.excerpt: The sn_cmdb_editor and app_service_user roles replace the itil role within the app_service_admin role.

questions.question: In Brazil, a CI data owner wants to restart the certification process for a CMDB certification task, so they reset the task. What happens to the task's results and comments?

options.text: Results go to 'Review not completed'; comments are removed
The task closes and a new task is created for the same CIs
Results are kept and the percent complete number returns to zero
Comments are kept and failed results go back for review

explanation.correct: The Brazil release notes describe resetting a certification task to restart the certification process: reset sets all certification results for the task to a 'Review not completed' state and removes any comments that were added. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Reset restarts the certification process for the same task; the notes do not describe closing it and generating a new task.
Reset does not keep the results; it sets all certification results for the task to 'Review not completed'.
Reset removes any comments that were added and resets all certification results, not just failed ones.

source.excerpt: Reset sets all certification results for the task to a 'Review not completed' state and removes any comments that were added.

questions.question: An administrator setting up a new Brazil instance reads that CMDB Baseline is being prepared for future deprecation. What does that mean, and what provides the latest experience for this functionality?

options.text: Removed at upgrade; CMDB 360 provides the latest experience
Hidden on new instances but supported; Unified Map replaces it
Activated on new instances but unsupported; Dependency Views replace it
Moved to a Store app; CMDB Query Builder provides the latest experience

explanation.correct: The Brazil deprecation notes state that CMDB Baseline will be hidden and no longer activated on new instances but will continue to be supported, and that Unified Map provides the latest experience for this functionality. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: CMDB Baseline is not removed; it continues to be supported. The CMDB release notes also list no CMDB removals, and the documented successor is Unified Map.
It is the reverse: CMDB Baseline will no longer be activated on new instances but will continue to be supported. Dependency Views are listed in the same deprecation entry, not as the replacement.
The notes do not move CMDB Baseline to a Store app, and they name Unified Map, not CMDB Query Builder, as the latest experience.

source.excerpt: Starting with the Brazil release, CMDB Baseline is being prepared for future deprecation. It will be hidden and no longer activated on new instances but will continue to be supported. Unified Map provides the latest experience for this functionality.

questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, a Data Catalog administrator creates a metadata collector connection and leaves the routing choice unchanged. Where does the connection run?

options.text: On the MID Server with the most free capacity
In the ServiceNow hosted cloud infrastructure
On a MID Server the collector owner picks per run
On the data source host through a local agent

explanation.correct: The 'MID Server routing for metadata collectors' feature (listed for Australia and Brazil) lets you choose whether a connection runs in the ServiceNow hosted cloud infrastructure, which is the default, or through a MID Server to reach your data sources. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-datacatalog-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: MID Server routing applies only when a collector is configured to run on a MID Server, and even then the default Auto-select model picks any available MID Server; the default connection runs in the hosted cloud.
When a MID Server is used, a routing model set by an administrator applies to all runs; the collector owner does not pick a MID Server for each run, and the default is the hosted cloud.
The documented options are the ServiceNow hosted cloud (default) or a MID Server; running on the data source host is not one of them.

source.excerpt: Choose whether a connection runs in the ServiceNow hosted cloud infrastructure (the default) or through a MID Server to reach your data sources.

questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, a data owner wants a Snowflake metadata collector in Data Catalog to classify the columns it harvests. Which service does the collector use for this?

options.text: ServiceNow Vault
Data Quality API
Zero Copy Connectors
Platform Analytics

explanation.correct: The 'Data classification with Vault' feature (Australia and Brazil) lets you enable a metadata collector to classify harvested columns using ServiceNow Vault; Snowflake is one of the collector types that support Vault classification. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-datacatalog-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Data Quality API is how external data quality tools submit rule results to Data Catalog; it does not classify harvested columns.
Zero Copy Connectors access data from external systems in place without replication (a Data products feature); they do not classify harvested columns.
Platform Analytics artifacts are something the ServiceNow metadata collector can harvest; Platform Analytics is not the classification service for harvested columns.

source.excerpt: Enable a metadata collector to classify harvested columns using ServiceNow Vault.

questions.question: A data engineer on Australia is building a data interface that combines several source tables. Which two operations do data interfaces support for multi-source composition? (Choose two.)

options.text: UNION
JOIN
PIVOT
MERGE

explanation.correct: The Australia Data products release notes state that data interfaces support multi-source composition through UNION and JOIN operations, and the highlights say governed data interfaces can be created from single tables, JOIN operations, or UNION operations using the Data Workbench wizard. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-dataproducts-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: PIVOT is not listed; the release notes name only UNION and JOIN operations for multi-source composition.
MERGE is not listed; data interfaces are created from single tables, JOIN operations, or UNION operations.

source.excerpt: Data interfaces support multi-source composition through UNION and JOIN operations

questions.question: On Australia, an administrator edits a published data interface to add columns and swap a source table. What happens to the consumers already using that interface?

options.text: They are disconnected and must request access to it again
They keep using it and must reconnect to get the changes
They receive the structural changes with no action
The edit is blocked until every consumer disconnects

explanation.correct: The Australia change 'Edit a published data interface' lets you add columns, swap source tables, change the combination method, update column mappings, or adjust join conditions; existing consumers continue to use the interface and must reconnect to pick up structural changes. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-dataproducts-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Existing consumers are not disconnected; they continue to use the interface.
Consumers do not get structural changes automatically; they must reconnect to pick them up.
The edit is allowed on a published interface while consumers continue to use it; nothing blocks it until consumers disconnect.

source.excerpt: Existing consumers continue to use the interface and must reconnect to pick up structural changes.

questions.question: A customer that uses Service Graph Connector Integration for Claroty CTD upgrades to Australia, where the app is being prepared for future deprecation. What does that mean for the app?

options.text: It is uninstalled automatically during the upgrade
It is hidden from installation but still supported
It stays installable but is no longer supported
It is replaced automatically by a newer connector

explanation.correct: Starting with the Australia release, the Service Graph Connector Integration for Claroty CTD application is being prepared for future deprecation: the app is hidden and can no longer be installed, but it is still supported. The Brazil notes repeat the same status. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-servicegraphconnectorintegrationforclarotyctd-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes do not uninstall the app; existing customers continue to be supported.
It is the reverse: the app is no longer available for installation but continues to be supported.
The release notes describe hiding the app while it continues to be supported; they do not describe an automatic replacement.

documentation.section: Service Graph Connector Integration for Claroty CTD - Deprecations

source.excerpt: Starting with the Australia release, the Service Graph Connector Integration for Claroty CTD application is being prepared for future deprecation.

questions.question: After upgrading to Australia, an administrator's JDBC data source for MSSQL fails because the mssql-jdbc.7.4.1.jre8 jar file is no longer part of the MID Server distribution. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Nothing; the MID Server downloads the jar file itself
Install that jar file or the vendor-recommended jar
Turn on parallel export sets for the data source
Configure a connection alias for the JDBC source

explanation.correct: The Australia Import and Export change says that if you have a JDBC data source integration that uses this jar file (that is, any MSSQL connections), install this jar file or the vendor recommended jar file according to KB0862383. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-importandexport-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The jar file is no longer part of the MID Server distribution, and the notes tell you to install it or the vendor recommended jar; they do not say the MID Server fetches it.
Parallel export sets are a separate Australia feature for exporting data with multiple small attachments in parallel; they do not supply the missing JDBC driver.
A connection alias is a separate Australia feature that lets you reuse connection settings across JDBC data sources; it does not supply the missing jar file.

source.excerpt: If you have a JDBC data source integration that uses this jar file (that is, any MSSQL connections) install this jar file or the vendor recommended jar file according to KB0862383.

questions.question: An integration architect on Australia needs external applications to receive inserts, updates, and deletes from selected ServiceNow tables in real time through Kafka. What does Integration Hub Stream Producer do?

options.text: Imports Kafka messages into import sets on a schedule
Streams table changes captured by CDC to Kafka topics
Replicates Kafka messages between clusters via Stream Connect
Exports table data to Kafka as nightly batch files

explanation.correct: Australia introduced Stream Producer, which automatically streams changes from ServiceNow tables to Kafka topics. It uses change data capture (CDC) technology to capture inserts, updates, and deletes on selected tables, formats them as messages, and sends them to a Kafka topic for real-time data synchronization with external applications. See https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-integrationhub-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Stream Producer sends data out of ServiceNow to Kafka topics; it does not import Kafka messages into import sets.
Stream Connect message replication (with OAUTHBEARER authentication added in Australia) is a separate capability; Stream Producer streams ServiceNow table changes to a Kafka topic.
Stream Producer captures changes with CDC and sends them as messages for real-time synchronization, not as nightly batch files.

source.excerpt: Stream Producer uses change data capture (CDC) technology to capture inserts, updates, and deletes on selected tables.
